summary: An old version of the IMP and TIP preventive maintenance schedule, replaced by RFC 638.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 633 publishes the monthly preventive maintenance schedule for ARPANET IMPs and TIPs. It warns that some machines may need to be taken down during maintenance and reserves Tuesday mornings for network software maintenance.

questions: when were arpanet imps and tips scheduled for maintenance
what time was reserved for network software maintenance
subtitle: A monthly preventive maintenance schedule for ARPANET IMP and TIP machines.

tldr.problem: Network users needed to know when IMP and TIP machines were scheduled for preventive maintenance and might be unavailable.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC lists monthly maintenance windows by week, day, site, and Eastern Time, and describes how schedule changes would be handled.
tldr.outcome: RFC 633 is an informational maintenance schedule and was obsoleted by RFC 638.

facts.label: Reserved software maintenance window
facts.value: Tuesday, 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. Eastern Time

today: RFC 633 is a preventive maintenance schedule and was obsoleted by RFC 638.

sections.title: How the Maintenance Schedule Works
sections.content:
Preventive maintenance is scheduled monthly, and a machine is normally scheduled at the same time each month. Where possible, the schedule coincides with preventive maintenance for the host or hosts at that site.

Maintenance normally does not require taking an IMP or TIP down, but the RFC warns that machines must be taken down in some cases. Users should not rely on a machine remaining available during its maintenance period.
sections.plainLanguage: Each machine usually has the same maintenance time every month. It may stay online, but the RFC warns users not to count on that.

sections.title: Maintenance Windows
sections.content:
The schedule is arranged by week of the month and weekday, with each site followed by a time window. All listed times are Eastern Time. For example, the RFC lists BBN IMP maintenance on the first Monday from 0830 to 1130 and UCLA maintenance on the third Monday from 1000 to 1300.

Tuesday mornings from 7 a.m. to 9 a.m. are reserved for network software maintenance.
sections.plainLanguage: The table gives each site's maintenance day and time in Eastern Time. Tuesday mornings from 7 to 9 are reserved for network software maintenance.

sections.title: Rescheduling Maintenance
sections.content: Network connectivity or other reasons may require a preventive maintenance change. BBN says it will use the usual procedure to schedule downtime with the site's primary contact. Permanent schedule changes will be announced through the RFC process.
sections.plainLanguage: If maintenance needs to move, BBN will coordinate downtime with the site's primary contact. Permanent changes will be announced in an RFC.
